items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the executive law, the public authorities law and the county
law, in relation to requiring certain documents and forms to be provided in
multiple languages
items.lawCode: Add Art 49-C §996, Exec L; add Art 9 Title 13 §2988, Pub Auth L; add Art 24-A §950, County L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5236             Revised 3/22/2021

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, the public authorities law and the
county law, in relation to requiring certain documents and forms to be
provided in multiple languages

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of the bill is to further expand language access in New York
State SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Explains the current necessity for expanded language access
in the forms of document translation and interpretation of government
services and resources as New York's immigrant population continues to
grow

Section 2. Amends the executive law by adding new article 49-c estab-
lishing the provisions of language access expansion with subsections 1-5
of section 996 of the executive law specifying the following:

Subsection 1. Explains the language access requirements of state agen-
cies who provide direct public services

Subsection 2. Sets the additional translation requirement established by
article eleven of the economic development law

Subsection 3. Sets the requirement that the list of most common
languages be updated biannually based on the census bureau's American
community survey

Subsection 4. Sets the requirement that each agency shall provide inter-
pretation services in the primary language of the individual in the
provision of services or benefits

Subsection 5. Sets the language access plan publishing process and
protocol

Section 3. Amends article 9 by adding a new title 13 establishing the
provisions of language access expansion with subsections 1-4 of section
2988 of the public authorities law specifying the following:  Subsection
1. Explains the language access requirements of state agencies who
provide direct public services Subsection 2. Sets the requirement that
the list of most common languages be updated at least biannually based
on the most recent census bureau's American community survey Subsection
3. Sets the requirement that each agency shall provide interpretation
services in the primary language of the individual in the provision of
services or benefits Subsection 4. Sets the language access plan
publishing process and protocol

Section 4. Amends the county law by adding a new article 24-A establish-
ing the provisions of language access expansion with subsections 1-4 of
section 950 of the county law specifying the following:

Subsection 1. Sets the requirement that political entities are to trans-
late vital documents in the twelve most common languages of the state
within the past five years
Subsection 2. Sets the potentiality for the addition of languages

Subsection 3. Sets the requirement that the list of most common
languages be updated at least biannually based on the most recent census
bureau's American community survey

Subsection 4. Sets the requirement that each agency shall provide inter-
pretation services in the primary language of the individual in the
provision of services or benefits

Section 5. Sets the effective date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Although New York State took the prior initiative toward expanding
language access in Governor Cuomo's Executive Order No. 26 in 2011,
which ordered all executive state agencies to translate vital documents
to 6 statewide languages, the lack of language access remains one of the
most significant barriers that New York's immigrant communities face
when trying to access critical state services. The necessity engendered
by this issue has been made more apparent with the ongoing COVID-19
pandemic, as only 6 of the most common languages spoken by individuals
with limited english proficiency (LEPs) are currently covered by Gover-
nor Cuomo's 2011 executive order. Expanding this to 12 languages would
be a much needed inclusive measure in overloaded agencies such as the
Department of Motor Vehicles and the Department of Education, which
immigrant populations often struggle to navigate.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

TBD

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Requires certain documents and forms to be provided in the twelve most common non-English languages spoken by limited English proficient immigrants of five years or less according to the American community survey, as published by the United States census bureau.
